# Templates

Arrange components by filling a template's slots. Use patterns to guide the choices.

**Kind:** Template

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/storybook-docs/templates/TemplatesOverview.mdx`

## The nine templates

Templates run from broadest to smallest. Each page covers types, anatomy, key states and usage. See Templates and patterns below for how the layers fit together.

- **Frame.** The app frame: the Sidebar beside the Page, with the AI panel as its own region. Three types: default, focused and bare.
- **Page.** The content inside a Frame: a page header, then Sections on the 12-column grid. Two types: default and full width.
- **Section.** A span of the page grid under one heading: a header, a body, and an optional side, detail and footer.
- **Card.** A raised container for one object on a page, such as a student, a session or a metric: an optional image, a header over a body, and an optional footer.
- **Table.** How a table sits on a page: the Section header carries the title and toolbar, and the table spans the section under it.
- **Form.** A stack of fields with a footer, in one of four places: in a page, in a Panel, in a Modal, or in steps.
- **Modal.** One task before anything else can happen, centered over a Backdrop. Four types: Passive, Active, Acknowledge and Steps.
- **Panel.** A full-height layer beside or over the Page with no Backdrop. Two floating types: Details and Notifications.
- **Popup.** A floating layer that hangs off its trigger and closes on an outside click. Six types, from menu to stacked filter menu.

## Templates and patterns

Templates define slots; patterns guide decisions across templates.

### Three layers

Fill a template's slots; consult a pattern when choosing or reconsidering an approach. Each layer owns one kind of guidance.

- **Components** are single pieces with props, imported by name. The question is "Am I using this piece right?" Anatomy is the piece's parts.
- **Templates** are arrangements of components with slots. They hold key scenarios and key states, and link to components for detail. The question is "Are the slots filled right?" Anatomy is the numbered slots.
- **Patterns** are code-free guidance for a situation, shown on annotated templates used as they are or tweaked. The question is "Is this the right approach?" A pattern has no anatomy and no code.

### The tie-break

Behavior splits out into a component, and a template that only redraws one component stays a component. One component's behavior goes on the component page. How pieces sit in one template goes on that template's page. Anything that holds across two or more templates is a pattern.

The step up from a quick look to its own page is under Opening a record, below. A rule lives in one place. A template page that needs a pattern's rule links to it and keeps its own words for the slots.

### Frame, Screen, Flow

- **Frame:** the template. Sidebar, Page and the AI panel slot, in its default, focused and bare types.
- **Screen:** a Frame with its slots filled for one page. Screens are documented under Flows in Figma.
- **Flow:** Screens in order, fulfilling one user story. Flows are documented under Flows in Figma as well.

## Which template for which job

A suggested starting point for each scenario, with the patterns to consult and the components it is built from. Never "always use". To start from the situation instead, use the Patterns overview.

| Scenario | Template | Patterns | Components |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| An area page with one collection | Page · default, with a Section view bar alone | Filtering · Search · Common actions | `PageHeader`, `Tabs` (pill), `FilterButton`, `IconButton`, `Button`, `Table` |
| A home page with several Sections | Page · default, titled Sections, cards | Empty · Loading | `PageHeader`, `Card`, `Button` |
| A record page, one level down | Page with a breadcrumb and page tabs | Navigation · Indicators | `Breadcrumb`, `PageHeader`, `StatusTag`, `Tabs`, `PopupSelect` |
| Working through a queue | Section with a detail | Navigation · Common actions | `Table`, `Button` |
| A quick look at one row | Panel · Details | Navigation | `Panel`, `Button` |
| A short decision before going on | Modal · Active, confirm width | Common actions · Errors | `Modal`, `Button` |
| A long task with steps | Frame · focused, with a Form in steps | Forms · Navigation | `ProgressTracker`, `Fieldset`, `Button` |
| Settings saved as a group | Form in a page, on the Page under its page-level header; subsections for several groups | Forms · Read-only · Disabled | `Fieldset`, `TextField`, `PopupSelect`, `Toggle`, `Button` |
| Narrowing a long catalog | Section with a filter side | Filtering | `Checkbox`, `PopupSelect`, `Button` |
| Signing in | Frame · bare | Forms · Errors | `Logo`, `TextField`, `Button` |
| Notifications | Panel · Notifications (the Inbox) | Notifications | `Panel`, `Avatar`, `PopupSelect` |
| AI chat | Frame, the AI panel region | AI interaction guidelines | `AiChat`, `PromptInput`, `AiMessage` |

## Frame, Modal, Panel or Popup?

One chooser for the four layers that take over from the page or sit above it. A filled dot means the layer is built for it.

| The task… | Frame · focused | Modal | Panel | Popup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| blocks the page until it is done | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| keeps the page in view and usable | No | No | Yes | Yes |
| holds a long task, or five or more steps | Yes | No | No | No |
| holds a short sequence of steps | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| takes a form | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| is a destructive confirm | No | Yes | No | No |
| hangs off its trigger | No | No | No | Yes |
| dims the page under a Backdrop | No | Yes | No | No |
| has its own URL | Yes | No | No | No |
| closes on Escape and returns focus | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |

A Panel that needs full attention becomes a Modal. Anything wider than 4-col, or that outlives a click, leaves the Popup for a Panel. Leaving a focused task goes through Close or Cancel, and unsaved work asks first, in a Modal.

## Opening a record

Least room to most. Pick the lowest step that fits; Navigation holds the rule.

Where a message sits, in a Frame, Page or Section banner, a Flag or a SectionMessage, is Notifications.
